business_rules: A shipment must have origin, destination, and delivery deadline at registration (RF-0, RF-06).
Each shipment receives a unique tracking identifier (RF-02).
Shipment origin and destination must differ (RF-03).
Origin remains fixed throughout the logistics lifecycle (RF-04).
Registration may complete before a route is defined; such shipments are 'unrouted' (RF-05, RF-11).
Origin/destination selectable only from previously registered locations (RF-07).
A candidate route is valid only if it satisfies origin, final destination, and delivery deadline (RF-09).
When no route meets criteria, the system informs the user no feasible option exists (RF-12).
A changed destination must not equal the shipment's origin or current destination (RF-15).
Changing destination triggers route reassessment; incompatible routes require a new routing decision (RF-16, RF-17).
Every logistics event must be associated with an existing shipment, location, and (for loading/unloading) trip (RF-32, RF-33, RF-34).
Non-loading/unloading events do not require a trip identifier (RF-35).
Events referencing non-existent shipment, location, or trip must be rejected (RF-36).
Recording a valid event updates shipment operational status and recalculates status/location/next step/plan adherence (RF-37, RF-38).
An event differing from the planned route marks the shipment as off route (RF-39).
Unloading at final destination marks the shipment as arrived (RF-40).
Recording recipient pickup marks the shipment logistically complete (RF-41).
No invalid event may alter shipment state (RNF-47).
Origin/destination/deadline/route-compatibility rules applied uniformly across all channels (RNF-48).
Shipment status recalculated on any relevant planning or execution change (RNF-49).
Each event retains both occurrence time and recording time (RNF-51).
The tracking model is unique regardless of channel (RNF-67).
